title: First Columbia recordings in New Orleans and the baseball and foot-stomping problems
summary: The Owls' first electronic recordings were made in the Godchaux Building; playback picked up radio baseball scores and then their stomping, so they removed their shoes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Just about the time of the recording. We had to send it in a little prior to the recording, as I recall, because they wouldn't record it unless it was copyrighted. And that was one of our first recordings. That together with a piece called Oh Me, Oh My, which none of us had written, but was just a sheet of music that we happened to have and were playing at that time. And that was our very, very first recordings, which were made here in New Orleans in the old Godshaw Building. They came down here, I think, from Atlanta. Columbia Recording sent people down here from Atlanta. And we went up to the Godshaw Building to make these recordings. It was quite an event for us at that time, I'll say. We enjoyed it very much. And, of course, now it sounds more or less just like the old-time recordings. I don't think their electronic recordings were at it best at that time. As I recall, that was some of the first electronic recordings that were made.
You were telling us about some trouble you had with the recording.

Well, when we made the recording, as I recall, they played it back principally to find out if we were seated right, to see whether the balance between the various instruments was correct. When they played it back, the predominant sound that came from the record was the baseball scores, which were being broadcast by WSMB at that time. Of course, that altered everything. They had to go to work and see if they could get that out of there, which they did. And then we made another trial run. And when they played that back, I'd say the thing that overpowered the music more than anything else was the stomping of our feet. And after we all removed our shoes and cushioned that, then we got the recording across. And it finally came out as, I think, as they expected it to, or hoped it would anyway.
